overall_summary: Analysis of the initial 9 shorts shows a standout outlier in the husband-wife relationship category (1,550 views), while parent-related emotional shorts (Maa and Papa) perform moderately well (139-224 views). Pure sibling content underperformed compared to family dynamics involving deeper emotional labor or partner relationships.

winning_patterns.evidence: Wife emotional video reached 1,550 views, and Maa video reached 224 views.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on domestic relationships, partnerships, and parental sacrifices that evoke heavy emotional guilt or gratitude.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles using direct second-person address ('आज किसी अपने को Call कर लेना') gained stable traction (288 views).
winning_patterns.action: Keep using titles that talk directly to the viewer about personal actions and unexpressed feelings.

weak_patterns.evidence: Both sister-focused shorts generated very low views (16 and 114 views respectively).
weak_patterns.action: Pause repetitive sister appreciation shorts and pivot toward broader relationship friction or nocturnal overthinking.

next_video.hook_style: Direct real-life observation about modern life distance
next_video.concept: A short about how busy we get with our phones, ignoring the person sitting right next to us until they stop complaining.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with the sound of notification rings and a person scrolling endlessly while their partner/parent waits to speak.
next_video.twist_direction: The moment they finally put the phone down to talk, the room is already empty of that attention.
next_video.reason: Aligns with the top-performing relationship/partner theme and captures the evening overthinking and family time window.

experiment: Testing if shifting from broad family tributes to direct partner/relationship regret (similar to the top-performing wife video) sustains higher baseline views.
